questions.question: What is the primary aim of a computer network?
options: To share resources among various connected devices
To increase the physical size of computing hardware
To eliminate the need for transmission media
To convert all digital communications into analog formats
questions.explanation: The main goal of a computer network is to allow various connected devices to share resources with each other.

questions.question: Which combination of networks historically came together to form the public Internet?
options: LAN, MAN, and PAN
ARPANET, NSFNET, and Private Networks
Only ARPANET and NSFNET without private systems
A collection of local telephone exchange lines
questions.explanation: As shown in the evolution diagram, the Internet was formed by combining ARPANET, NSFNET, and various Private Networks.

questions.question: If a network is set up for an individual person and covers an area of up to 30 feet (about 10 meters), what type of network is it?
options: Local Area Network (LAN)
Personal Area Network (PAN)
Metropolitan Area Network (MAN)
Wide Area Network (WAN)
questions.explanation: A Personal Area Network (PAN) is arranged within an individual person, typically covering an area of 10 meters or 30 feet.

questions.question: Which hardware component is absolutely necessary to physically connect a computer over a network?
options: Network Interface Card (NIC)
Repeater
Bridge
Gateway
questions.explanation: A Network Interface Card (NIC) is a circuit board installed in a computer that provides a dedicated network connection, and without it, a computer cannot connect over a network.

questions.question: How does a modem allow a computer to send digital data over analog telephone lines?
options: It amplifies the digital signal so it can travel longer distances
It converts the computer's digital signal into an analog signal, and vice versa
It broadcasts the digital signal directly into the air as radio waves
It forces the telephone lines to accept pure digital pulses
questions.explanation: A modem converts a computer's digital data into analog data (using a modulator) when sending, and converts analog signals back to digital data (using a demodulator) when receiving.

questions.question: Why is a switch considered more efficient than a hub in a network?
options: A switch broadcasts incoming data to all connected devices on the network
A switch shares a single collision domain among all connected ports
A switch selectively forwards data only to the intended recipient based on MAC addresses
A switch only operates at the physical layer, avoiding complex processing
questions.explanation: A switch learns MAC addresses and selectively forwards frames to the correct destination port, whereas a hub simply replicates and broadcasts data to every connected device.

questions.question: In which transmission mode can both connected devices transmit and receive data at the exact same time, like a telephone call?
options: Simplex Mode
Half-Duplex Mode
Full-Duplex Mode
Semi-Simplex Mode
questions.explanation: In full-duplex mode, both stations can transmit and receive simultaneously, allowing real-time, two-way communication.

questions.question: If a network has a maximum capacity of 100 Mbps but is currently transmitting 80 Mbps of data successfully, what are its bandwidth and throughput?
options: Bandwidth is 80 Mbps, Throughput is 100 Mbps
Bandwidth is 100 Mbps, Throughput is 80 Mbps
Bandwidth is 100 Mbps, Latency is 80 ms
Both Bandwidth and Throughput are 100 Mbps
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the maximum theoretical capacity (100 Mbps), while throughput is the actual amount of data successfully transmitted (80 Mbps).

questions.question: Why does Manchester encoding require almost double the bandwidth of NRZ (Non-Return-to-Zero) encoding?
options: Manchester encoding uses twice as many voltage levels
Manchester encoding requires two separate physical cables
Manchester encoding always contains a transition in the middle of each bit
Manchester encoding only transmits analog wave signals
questions.explanation: Because Manchester encoding always includes a transition in the middle of every bit for synchronization, it requires almost double the bandwidth of NRZ.

questions.question: Which function of the Data Link Layer is used to synchronize sender and receiver speeds to prevent a slow receiver's buffer from overflowing?
options: Access Control
Routing
Flow Control
Framing
questions.explanation: Flow control is the mechanism used by the Data Link Layer to maintain a constant, compatible data rate between both sides so that a fast sender does not overwhelm a slow receiver's buffer.
